en: The Philippines officially has 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the previously taught number of 7,107.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through northern Luzon.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Taal Volcano holds the record for the most historical eruptions in the Philippines, with 34 recorded events.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines, covering a total land area of 14,649 square kilometers.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the world's smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in body length.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an underground river that stretches 8.2 kilometers long.
The Chocolate Hills of Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped hills spread over 50 square kilometers.
Tinuy-an Falls in Bislig is often called the Little Niagara of the Philippines, dropping 55 meters across three tiers.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of over 3,800 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the Philippines.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
